真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 18 页

Q7：Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage. Q12–13：TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN。

原文第8段Commentators have often described the sisters as unlikely pioneer collectors. Much is made of their isolation in rural Wales and the fact that they didn't make friends with artists or gallery owners. Yet they didn't feel obliged to follow fashionable tastes and were free to pursue their own preferences. Although they relied on a trusted circle of advisers, they made frequent trips to London and Paris, and also regularly had paintings sent to their home for consideration.

原文第9段By the early 1920s, Gwendoline felt increasingly uncomfortable buying art works when faced with the poverty and social upheaval created by the First World War. Her philanthropic pursuits then became focused almost exclusively on social causes and the development of the sisters' home at Gregynog Hall into a conference center and venue for the Gregynog Festival of Music and Poetry. Gwendoline made her final art purchase in March 1926. Margaret also stopped collecting around this time, but started again in the 1930s acquiring, on a relatively small scale, work by contemporary British artists.

原文第10段The sisters collected French Impressionist paintings at a time when such art was routinely ignored by individuals and institutions alike. The Gwendoline and Margaret Davies collection, donated in 1951 and 1963 respectively to the National Museum Wales, contains major examples of work by leading French Impressionists. In collecting paintings that they loved, the sisters created a lasting and meaningful cultural legacy for the people of Wales and beyond.

第 7 题作答

12. The impact of the First World War encouraged Gwendoline to reconsider her interest in collecting art.

第 12 题作答

13. The Davies sisters bought French Impressionist art during a period when very few people were doing so.

Much is made of their isolation in rural Wales and the fact that they didn't make friends with artists or gallery owners. Yet they didn't feel obliged to follow fashionable tastes and were free to pursue their own preferences. Although they relied on a trusted circle of advisers, they made frequent trips to London and Paris, and also regularly had paintings sent to their home for consideration.评论者常把姐妹描述为出人意料的收藏先驱，因为她们住在威尔士乡间，也不与艺术家或画廊主人交朋友。作者随后补充另一面：远离潮流压力使她们能够追随自己的品味。她们仍依赖可信顾问，经常到伦敦和巴黎，也让人把画送到家里考虑，因此地理上的偏远不等于缺少接触作品的机会。原文第9段By the early 1920s, Gwendoline felt increasingly uncomfortable buying art works when faced with the poverty and social upheaval created by the First World War. Her philanthropic pursuits then became focused almost exclusively on social causes and the development of the sisters' home at Gregynog Hall into a conference center and venue for the Gregynog Festival of Music and Poetry. Gwendoline made her final art purchase in March 1926. Margaret also stopped collecting around this time, but started again in the 1930s acquiring, on a relatively small scale, work by contemporary British artists.到1920年代初，战争遗留的贫困和社会动荡使格温多琳对继续购画越来越不安。她把精力几乎完全转向社会事业，并将家宅发展为会议及音乐诗歌节场所，1926年作了最后一次购画。玛格丽特也在大致同期停止收藏，却在1930年代恢复小规模购买当代英国作品。两人的后续选择有关联，但不能合并为完全相同的人生轨迹。原文第10段The sisters collected French Impressionist paintings at a time when such art was routinely ignored by individuals and institutions alike. The Gwendoline and Margaret Davies collection, donated in 1951 and 1963 respectively to the National Museum Wales, contains major examples of work by leading French Impressionists. In collecting paintings that they loved, the sisters created a lasting and meaningful cultural legacy for the people of Wales and beyond.文章把个人经历放回当时的艺术接受环境：姐妹收藏印象派时，个人和机构普遍忽视这类作品。她们的藏品后来分别于1951年和1963年捐给威尔士国家博物馆，包含重要画家的代表作。最后一句评价她们追随个人喜爱的行为产生了超出私人范围的长期文化价值。词语与搭配free to pursue their own preferences能够自由追随自己的喜好be free to强调不受外部义务或压力束缚；这里与不必追随流行趣味相连，不表示完全不接受建议。when faced with the poverty and social upheaval面对贫困和社会动荡时when faced with是省略主语和be动词的结构，后接所面对的局面；说明价值判断发生变化的社会背景。on a relatively small scale以相对较小的规模scale描述活动的规模，relatively保留比较意味；这里限定玛格丽特后来恢复收藏的程度。a lasting and meaningful cultural legacy持久且有意义的文化遗产legacy是前人行动留给后来者的影响或成果；这里不是遗产金额，而是可被公众持续接触的艺术收藏。句子精读Although they relied on a trusted circle of advisers, they made frequent trips to London and Paris, and also regularly had paintings sent to their home for consideration.虽然她们依靠一群信赖的顾问，但仍经常前往伦敦和巴黎，也常让人把画送到家中供她们考虑。Although引出依靠顾问的事实，主句突出她们自己的主动参与。made frequent trips和had paintings sent并列；have something done表示安排别人完成某事，sent是过去分词。for consideration说明送画是为了供她们考察是否购买，而非已经购入。The Gwendoline and Margaret Davies collection, donated in 1951 and 1963 respectively to the National Museum Wales, contains major examples of work by leading French Impressionists.格温多琳和玛格丽特·戴维斯的收藏分别于1951年和1963年捐给威尔士国家博物馆，其中包括法国重要印象派画家的代表作品。主干是collection contains major examples。donated...是插入的过去分词短语，补充藏品的捐赠去向和时间；respectively将两位姐妹按姓名顺序与两个年份对应。by leading French Impressionists修饰work，leading在这里指具有重要地位，并非位置靠前。这篇材料里可用于写作的表达a lasting and meaningful cultural legacy持久且有意义的文化遗产可用于讨论文化活动对未来的贡献，但要写清通过什么机制传承，例如保留地方戏剧、作品或表演传统，不能只用抽象赞美代替解释。用于写作：直接服务于实体剧院的文化价值：说明现场演出空间如何承载和传递传统，而不只比较观看的便利程度。读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。
